prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Dallas for a truck accident case?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t honestly name a single “best” lawyer — that depends on your case facts and what you want (highest recovery, aggressive trial lawyer, quick settlement, etc.). I can, however, help you find the right top-tier Dallas truck‑accident lawyer and tell you how to evaluate them. If you want, I can also pull a short vetted list of 3–5 Dallas attorneys/firms — tell me your ZIP code and any priorities (trial experience, multilingual lawyer, low fee, etc.).

How to find the right Dallas truck‑accident lawyer
- Look for focused truck‑accident/commercial vehicle experience (not just general car-crash work). Truck cases involve federal rules (FMCSA), commercial carrier defenses, and different insurance/indemnity issues.
- Trial experience and trial results. Many claims are settled, but a lawyer who will and can try the case is more valuable in negotiations.
- Use of experts — accident reconstruction, logbook/ELD analysts, trucking industry experts, medical and life‑care planners.
- Board certification and memberships: Texas Board of Legal Specialization (personal injury trial law), Texas Trial Lawyers Association, and specialty recognitions (Super Lawyers, Best Lawyers, Martindale-Hubbell).
- Track record: past verdicts/settlements in truck cases. Look for representative results, not just marketing language.
- Communication and resources: will the lawyer personally handle your case? Do they have investigators and the budget to litigate against trucking companies?
- Fee structure and costs: most personal injury lawyers take cases on contingency (commonly 33–40% of recovery), but ask about how costs (expert fees, court costs) are handled.

Where to search and verify credentials
- State Bar of Texas — lawyer search and disciplinary history
- Texas Board of Legal Specialization — board‑certified personal injury trial lawyers
- Super Lawyers / Best Lawyers / Martindale-Hubbell / Avvo — client reviews and peer ratings
- Texas Trial Lawyers Association — membership indicates focus on plaintiff work

Important questions to ask in a free consultation
- How many truck (commercial vehicle) cases have you handled? How many tried to verdict?
- Do you handle cases in Dallas County courts and federal court (if applicable)?
- Can you give examples of recent truck‑accident settlements or verdicts (similar to my facts)?
- Who will handle day‑to‑day work — you or an associate? How do you communicate with clients?
- What experts will you use and how are those costs handled?
- What is your fee and how are litigation costs advanced/recouped?
- What is your strategy to preserve evidence (black box/ELD, driver logs, cargo manifests, witness statements)?
- Do you have experience with trucking company defenses (independent contractors, leasing companies, interstate regulatory issues)?

Timing and practical notes
- Texas generally has a 2‑year statute of limitations for personal injury — act promptly.
- Preserve evidence: take photos, get witness contact info, don’t give recorded statements to insurers without your lawyer.
- Ask for a consultation quickly; many strong injury firms offer free case evaluations.

If you want specific recommendations
Tell me your ZIP code and a brief summary of the accident (date, injuries, location, whether commercial truck involved, any known company or insurer). I’ll research and give a short list (3–5) of Dallas lawyers/firms that fit your needs plus the key reasons each might be a good match.
